sections.h2: Who sends a property tax bill to a Johnson City homeowner?
sections.html:
Two bills can arrive. The City of Johnson City Finance Department bills and collects the city tax, and the Washington County Trustee collects the county tax on the same parcel. The city's property tax page lists the Municipal and Safety Building at 601 E. Main St., open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Mail goes to P.O. Box 2227, Johnson City, TN 37605, and the tax office number for delinquent balances is 423-434-6299.

The county side runs through two other offices. The Assessor of Property at 423-753-1671 handles appraisal and mailing address questions, while the Trustee at 423-753-1602 only collects. The Trustee's county tax page says plainly that it does not appraise property or set the rate.

Johnson City sits mostly in Washington County, with smaller pieces in Carter and Sullivan counties. A house in one of those pieces answers to a different county assessor and trustee, so check the county shown on your parcel record before you call anyone.

sections.h2: When is Johnson City property tax due this year?
sections.html:
The city says 2026 notices went out the week of October 12, and payment is due by February 28, 2027. A postmark on or before that date counts, and penalty and interest start on March 1, 2027. The county notice follows a similar track: the Trustee mails in October, takes payment through the end of February, and adds 1.5% interest to unpaid balances on March 1.

Today is November 15, 2026, which is the date the county page names for a warning: an owner who has no county notice by November 15 should contact the Trustee at once. Tennessee owners are expected to pay whether or not a notice arrives. A homeowner whose lender pays from escrow will not receive a bill, so ask the servicer for proof of payment.

Ways to pay the city portion:

  • In person at 601 E. Main St. during weekday hours
  • By mail to the P.O. Box above
  • Online through the Finance Department's payment system, which adds a 2.75% processing fee per transaction

The city notes that online accounts past the due date are delinquent and cannot be paid online, and neither can taxes already filed in Chancery Court. For those balances call 423-434-6299 to confirm the exact payoff before sending money.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Johnson City, and how does that shape a sale?
sections.html:
Johnson City began in 1856 as a railroad stop called Johnson's Depot and was incorporated in 1869. Three rail lines crossed downtown at the peak, and the city later grew around East Tennessee State University, Ballad Health and the medical campus that includes Johnson City Medical Center and the VA hospital at Mountain Home. It sits in an Appalachian valley near Boone Lake on the Watauga River, and Buffalo Mountain, a ridge above 2,700 feet, is a city park on the south side.

Climate matters for older homes here. The city has a humid subtropical climate with about 45 inches of rain a year and roughly 16 inches of snow, so roofs, gutters and crawl spaces take steady moisture. The Johnson City Independent School District covers most of the city inside Washington County, with Science Hill High School and University School among its schools, and a few edges belong to the county school systems.

Census Bureau QuickFacts gives a picture of the housing stock:

  • 74,943 residents on July 1, 2025, up 5.5% from the 2020 base
  • Owner-occupied rate of 51.3%, so about half of households rent
  • Median owner-occupied home value of $268,200 for 2020 to 2024
  • Median gross rent of $1,023 and median household income of $57,254
  • 20.3% of residents in poverty

With roughly half the households renting, a Johnson City seller may be a landlord with tenants in place, and the city and county balances for that rental should be pulled before an offer is signed.

sections.h2: How is the Johnson City tax amount figured?
sections.html:
Tennessee taxes residential property at 25% of appraised value, and the rate is applied per $100 of that assessment. The Washington County Trustee's page works a $150,000 home: $37,500 of assessment times the county rate gives the bill, rounded to the nearest dollar since tax year 2020. Its table lists a county rate of $2.15 per $100 under the heading 2023, so treat that number as dated and read the rate off your own 2026 notice.

The city adds its own rate on top for houses inside Johnson City limits. The city page does not print the rate, so ask City Finance for the current figure. Washington County reappraised in 2024 according to the City of Kingsport's explanation of regional value changes, which means many owners saw a new appraisal that year, and the next county notice is where any later change appears.

sections.h2: What can I do if I think my Johnson City assessment is wrong?
sections.html:
Start with the Washington County Assessor of Property at 423-753-1671. Some assessors offer an informal review, but the Tennessee Comptroller says informal review is not an appeal. The formal first step is the county board of equalization, which meets in June, and a disputed assessment generally becomes final if it skips that board.

An owner who loses there can go to the State Board of Equalization by August 1 or within 45 days of the county board's notice, whichever is later. The state appeal page says the best evidence for a house is sales of comparable homes, with differences in size, age and condition explained. A bare claim that the home is overvalued is usually not enough, and a higher value after a countywide reappraisal does not by itself prove an error.

Pay at least the undisputed part of the bill before the delinquency date while the appeal is open, and pay any delinquent prior-year taxes in full.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when a Johnson City house is sold?
sections.html:
The county says the official tax roll reflects the owner on January 1, so the seller usually gets the bill even if the house sells in the fall. Taxes are normally prorated at closing, and the buyer becomes the responsible party after that. A closing agent asks the city and the Trustee for payoff figures and pays them from the seller's proceeds.

Where the bill is already delinquent, ask for the payoff from the tax office directly, because online balances may lag payments in transit. If the account has gone to Chancery Court, payment goes through the Clerk and Master and cannot be made on the city's website. A cash buyer who closes quickly can settle those balances at the table, which helps when an inherited or tenant-occupied house has fallen behind.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to pay Johnson City property tax for 2026?
faqs.a: February 28, 2027. The city honors a postmark on or before that date and starts penalty and interest on March 1, 2027. The county Trustee collects the county tax through the end of February as well.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Johnson City property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, for current balances. The city charges a 2.75% processing fee per transaction. Delinquent accounts and taxes filed in Chancery Court cannot be paid online, so call 423-434-6299 for the exact payoff.

faqs.q: Who do I call if I never got a county tax notice?
faqs.a: Call the Washington County Trustee at 423-753-1602. The county asks owners without a notice by November 15 to call right away, and the tax is owed even when no notice arrives.

faqs.q: Does Johnson City tax apply to houses in Carter or Sullivan County?
faqs.a: The city bills its own tax inside city limits in every county, but the county portion goes to that county's trustee. Look up the county on your parcel record and contact that county's assessor and trustee for dates and rates.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Johnson City house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid city and county balances are paid at closing from the seller's proceeds. Ask the tax office for the payoff amount first so the title company has a current number.
